correctness.rationale: For any order-three element \(g\), \(\operatorname{Cay}(G,\{g,g^{-1}\})\) is a disjoint union of right cosets of \(\langle g\rangle\), each a triangle. Thus the two witnesses in \(A_n\) give isomorphic graphs. The standard character has value \(|\mathrm{Fix}(g)|-1\), giving sums \(2(n-4)\) for a 3-cycle and \(2(n-7)\) for two disjoint 3-cycles. For \(n\ge7\) the standard irreducible is the unique degree-\(n-1\) character, so the degree-\(n-1\) character-sum sets are unequal. The low boundaries \(n=7,8\) were independently recomputed from the hook-length restriction/splitting rule; the general uniqueness is the classical small-degree character fact.
residual_risks: The theorem intentionally starts at \(n=7\); the character-degree uniqueness used here fails in the same form at \(A_6\).

originality.rationale: The 2015 primary paper proves non-invariance for symmetric groups and some additional groups, then ends by asking which nonabelian groups have the invariant; the accessible author-uploaded text and targeted searches did not reveal an alternating-group family. Non-BI status does not pass automatically from \(S_n\) to the index-two subgroup \(A_n\). Resultary returned the assigned \(A_n\) theorem as the exact hit, with the nearest BI result concerning \(\operatorname{AGL}(1,q)\), a different family. The explicit two-triangle witness inside \(A_n\) therefore survives implication comparison.
residual_risks: The complete searchable text of every page of the 2015 paper was not available through the current route; an unindexed alternating-group remark remains a bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The 2015 paper explicitly leaves BI-group classification open. A uniform counterfamily covering all alternating groups from \(A_7\) onward, witnessed by two size-two connection sets and a single natural character, is a motivated structural classification result even though the final construction is short.
residual_risks: The boundary groups \(A_5,A_6\) remain outside the theorem.

limitations: The witnesses are disconnected Cayley graphs, which is allowed by the BI definition used in the cited work.
